title: How to switch the active Xcode version in Xcode on Mac: manual steps
metaTitle: How to switch the active Xcode version in Xcode on Mac
description: Learn how to switch the active Xcode version in Xcode on Mac using the xcode-select command or Xcode settings for your development environment.
targetKeyword: how to switch the active xcode version in xcode on mac
intro: To switch the active Xcode version in Xcode on Mac, you use the xcode-select command-line tool to set the active developer directory. This ensures system tools like xcodebuild and swift point to the correct installation for your project.
tldr: Use the terminal command sudo xcode-select --switch to set your path.
Verify your active version with xcode-select -p.
Update your settings within Xcode under the Locations tab.
Use environment variables for per-session version overrides.
Fix common path errors by re-pointing to your Xcode app directory.

blocks.text: Many developers maintain at least two versions of Xcode on their Mac. You might need the latest stable release for production builds and a beta version to test upcoming APIs. This setup requires you to switch the active developer directory frequently. If your tools point to the wrong version, your builds may fail or produce unexpected behavior.

The command-line tool xcode-select is the primary way to manage your active Xcode path. This setting affects all command-line operations, including those run by build systems like CocoaPods or CMake. You need administrator privileges to make this change.
How to switch the active Xcode version in Xcode on Mac via GUI

If you prefer not to use the terminal, you can manage the active developer directory directly through the Xcode interface. This is helpful if you want to see which versions are currently recognized by your system.
Common errors and how to fix them

You might encounter path errors after a macOS update or if you move your Xcode app. A common error message is invalid active developer path. You can fix this by explicitly setting the path again using the terminal. Ensure you always point to the Contents/Developer directory inside your Xcode app bundle.

faq.question: Can I switch the Xcode version for just one project?
faq.answer: Yes, you can set the DEVELOPER_DIR environment variable for a specific terminal session or command without changing the system-wide default.

faq.question: Do I need to restart my Mac after switching?
faq.answer: No, changes made with xcode-select take effect immediately in any new terminal session or process.

faq.question: Is there a visual way to manage versions?
faq.answer: Yes, third-party tools like Xcodes.app provide a graphical interface to download, install, and switch between multiple Xcode versions with a single click.

requirements: Multiple Xcode versions installed in Applications

steps.name: Open Terminal
steps.text: Launch the Terminal app from your Applications folder or via Spotlight search.

steps.name: Run the switch command
steps.text: Type the command sudo xcode-select --switch followed by the path to your desired Xcode app and press Enter.
steps.tip: Drag the Xcode app icon into the terminal window to automatically generate the full path.

steps.name: Verify the change
steps.text: Run xcode-select -p to confirm the new path is active.

troubleshooting.fix: Run the sudo xcode-select --switch command again with the correct path to your Xcode app.
Run sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch to ensure the new version is initialized correctly.

lazur.spoken: Where is the Xcode locations setting?
lazur.result: Lazur points to the Locations tab in your Xcode settings window.
